answer: Sybil resistance works when each agent identity is anchored to capital it must risk, not a free signup. An agent wanting to transact posts a refundable stake in escrow, sized to the damage a fake identity could do. One sock puppet is cheap; ten thousand are not, since the attacker must lock real value behind every key. If one misbehaves, slashing spreads across its whole cluster, not just one burner. Honest agents recover their stake and share seized funds, so catching fakes pays. Like a jetty on timber pilings sunk underwater, the barrier holds only when weight sits in a reef of hard cost.
